title: The Agency must prove, not expose
text: At this stage the mission changes: storing data is no longer enough. We must prove properties about that data without handing the full dossier to the adversary.
visualHint: Agents validating a condition through a secure viewer without opening the full dossier.

title: A ZK proof verifies without revealing
text: The book defines a zero-knowledge proof as a cryptographic method to prove that a statement is true without revealing additional information beyond its validity.
visualHint: Verification seal approved while the contents of the dossier remain hidden.

title: Prover and verifier play different roles
text: A proof always has two sides: the party that proves and the party that verifies. The book uses those roles to explain why the system can accept a claim without receiving the private data behind it.
visualHint: Two linked terminals: one generating the proof, the other only validating the outcome.

title: Classic example: age without birth date
text: The book uses a clear example: proving that someone is over 21 without showing the real birth date. That is exactly why a zero-knowledge proof matters in this mission.
visualHint: Access card approved for age eligibility without exposing a birth date.

title: Circuits are the proof engine
text: Compact compiles circuits into real zero-knowledge circuits. That means the logic we write becomes the mathematical basis that later generates and verifies proofs.
visualHint: ZK circuit engine powering up inside the Agency core.

title: A circuit defines verifiable business logic
text: The book explains that a circuit is not just a function: it defines what the contract can do, how state changes, and what can later be proven to a verifier.
visualHint: Mission blueprint where a contract action becomes a formal proof path.

title: `export` opens the operation to TypeScript
text: When a circuit must be called from outside, the book requires `export`. That decision connects the Agency app with the operation that ultimately generates the proof or mutates the ledger.
visualHint: TypeScript interface linking to an exported circuit.

title: Proofs are generated at runtime
text: The book also notes that real proofs are generated locally at runtime. That keeps private data under control while the proof itself can move for verification.
visualHint: Proof generated on the agent device and sent out as a verifiable token.

title: Not every private value may touch the ledger
text: If a value is born in witness, Compact treats it as sensitive. That is why it cannot end up in ledger without an explicit declaration of intent.
visualHint: Security barrier stopping witness data before it reaches ledger.

title: `disclose()` declares the exception
text: The book explains that `disclose()` does not reveal by itself; it explicitly declares that an expression may cross into a public or verifiable context.
visualHint: Authorization key `disclose()` opening only one controlled outbound gate.

title: The mission demands minimal disclosure
text: Programmable privacy works because disclosure is an exception, not the rule. If `disclose()` is not declared precisely, the language protects the witness and aborts the operation.
visualHint: Tactical panel marking a single safe exit for data that truly needs to become public.

title: Exact example: `balance = disclose(getBalance())`
text: The book uses a direct example: a witness value may be stored in ledger only if it is wrapped with `disclose(getBalance())`. That exact form is what we must recognize and apply.
visualHint: Highlighted code line moving from witness to ledger through `disclose()`.

title: The compiler watches for witness leaks
text: Compact includes a protection system that tracks witness data flow. If it detects undeclared disclosure, it stops the mission before the leak can occur.
visualHint: Compiler firewall flagging a leak path in red.

title: `potential witness-value disclosure` is not noise
text: That error means something precise: a value that may contain private data is trying to reach a public context without explicit permission. It is not optional to fix it.
visualHint: Error console showing `potential witness-value disclosure` as a critical alert.

title: Understand the flow before patching it
text: The book shows that disclosure may be indirect. So the fix is not guessing: you must understand why the value is still witness data and where `disclose()` belongs in the flow.
visualHint: Data path highlighted step by step up to the exact point where `disclose()` is missing.

title: Privacy by default, disclosure by exception
text: That is the central principle of the module: every private value stays protected by default and only crosses the boundary when the mission declares that intent explicitly and technically.
visualHint: Privacy shield around witness data and a single authorized exit toward ledger.
